newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER OUT FOR MONTHS WITH ANKLE INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER OUT FOR MONTHS WITH ANKLE INJURY.

text.p: Newcastle and England striker Alan Shearer will be out of action for "months rather than weeks" with severely torn ankle ligaments, his manager Kenny Dalglish said on Sunday.
Shearer injured his right ankle in the last minute of Saturday's friendly against Chelsea and underwent an operation in Newcastle on Sunday.

Dalglish revealed the extent of the injury at a news conference at Everton's Goodison Park ground after watching his side lose 3-0 to Ajax in the Umbro International tournament. "He had an operation to repair torn ligaments and will be out for a wee while," said Dalglish. "It will be months rather than weeks."

The injury will mean the England captain will almost certainly miss his country's World Cup qualifier against Moldova at Wembley on September 10 and possibly the showdown against Italy in Rome on October 11.

He will also miss Newcastle's European Champions Cup preliminary round fixture against either Partizan Belgrade or Croatia Zagreb in August. The winner of the two-legged match qualifies for the Champions League.
It is the latest in a long line of injury setbacks for the 27-year-old, who missed periods of last season after undergoing two groin operations.

He suffered a severe knee ligament injury in December 1993 which brought his first season at Blackburn to an early end but bounced back the following season to score 34 goals and earn the Footballer of the Year award.
Shearer's absence could lead to Newcastle trying to stop the sale of striker Les Ferdinand to Tottenham, although the London club said on Saturday that the deal would go through.

Daniel Sugar, son of Tottenham chairman Alan, said on Saturday night: "Newcastle have signed an agreement saying they will sell us the player. If we agree personal terms and he passes a medical he will be our player."
